title: Career Roadmap: DevOps Trainee
summary: A DevOps Trainee learns to automate software delivery, manage application environments, monitor systems, and support reliable deployments. DevOps brings together software development, IT operations, infrastructure automation, testing, and system reliability.

facts.Current degree: B.Sc. Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics

blocks.text: A DevOps Trainee learns to automate software delivery, manage application environments, monitor systems, and support reliable deployments. DevOps brings together software development, IT operations, infrastructure automation, testing, and system reliability.
A B.Sc. in Cloud Computing or Big Data Analytics can provide a relevant foundation, especially when paired with Linux, networking, scripting, Git, cloud services, containers, and CI/CD pipelines.
The trainee role is usually an entry-level position in which you work under the guidance of experienced developers, cloud engineers, or platform engineers.
Primary objective
Help teams build, test, deploy, and operate applications consistently and efficiently.
Core competencies
Linux, networking, Git, scripting, cloud infrastructure, Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
Potential workplaces
Software companies, cloud service providers, IT consultancies, SaaS companies, startups, and enterprise technology teams.
Recommended undergraduate degree

B.Sc. Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics can support a DevOps career when the curriculum includes operating systems, networking, programming, databases, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure.
Related pathways include B.Sc. Computer Science, BCA, or other computing degrees supplemented with practical infrastructure and deployment projects.
DevOps hiring often emphasizes practical skills and troubleshooting ability. A specific degree title alone does not guarantee job eligibility.
Subjects to prioritize

rows.text: Understand processes, memory, permissions, services, and system resources.
Learn IP addressing, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, ports, routing, and connectivity troubleshooting.
Automate repetitive tasks using Python and Bash.
Build logical thinking and efficient automation.
Understand connections, backups, access controls, and application dependencies.
Learn virtual machines, storage, networking, identity, and managed services.
Understand development workflows, version control, and release practices.
Learn how applications communicate across services and machines.
Apply least privilege, secure credentials, patching, and access controls.
Interpret logs, metrics, alerts, and service health indicators.

blocks.text: Learning sequence

items.text: Stage 1 — Computing foundations

blocks.text: Learn Linux commands, file permissions, networking, Git, and basic Python or Bash scripting. Practise running and troubleshooting a small web application locally.

items.text: Stage 2 — Cloud and containers

blocks.text: Learn one cloud platform, deploy a basic application, understand Docker images and containers, and configure environment variables and application logs.

items.text: Stage 3 — Automation and operations

blocks.text: Build a CI/CD pipeline, introduce infrastructure as code, add monitoring, and document deployment and rollback procedures.
For a three- or four-year degree, use coursework and projects to develop these skills progressively rather than waiting until graduation to begin practical deployment work.
A DevOps Trainee should first understand how an application runs, how it is deployed, and how to diagnose failures. Learn the fundamentals before moving to complex cloud-native systems.
A. Linux, networking, and scripting

items.text: Use Linux commands, shell scripts, file permissions, services, processes, and logs.
Understand DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, ports, firewalls, and basic troubleshooting.
Learn Python or Bash for automating repetitive tasks.
Use Git and GitHub to manage code and configuration changes.

blocks.text: B. Containers and CI/CD

items.text: Docker — package applications and dependencies into containers.
GitHub Actions — automate builds, tests, and deployment workflows.
Learn image tagging, environment configuration, secrets, and deployment rollback.
Study Kubernetes after becoming comfortable with containers and networking.

blocks.text: C. Cloud, infrastructure, and monitoring

blocks.label: Choose one cloud platform
blocks.text: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud.

items.text: Learn Terraform for repeatable infrastructure configuration.
Explore Prometheus and Grafana for metrics and dashboards.
Understand IAM, network security, backups, logging, and cost monitoring.

blocks.text: Recommended beginner stack
You do not need to master all three major cloud providers or every DevOps tool to qualify for a trainee role.
Build projects that demonstrate that you can deploy, troubleshoot, and maintain applications—not just run commands from a tutorial.

rows.text: Deploy a small website to a Linux server
Automatically test and build an application when code is pushed
Package a simple API using Docker
Deploy a small application with controlled network access
Provision a test environment using Terraform
Track application availability, response time, and resource use
Back up sample data and document restoration steps

blocks.label: Best first project
blocks.text: Automated application deployment
Take a simple Python or Node.js web application and build a pipeline that:

items.text: Stores the source code in GitHub.
Runs basic automated tests when code is pushed.
Builds a Docker image.
Deploys the application to a test environment.
Verifies that the application is responding.
Records deployment logs and explains how to roll back a failed release.

blocks.text: Document the architecture, pipeline stages, setup steps, security decisions, and known limitations in a README.
Use a local environment or an appropriately secured free-tier cloud setup. Cloud services can incur charges, so configure budgets, alerts, and resource cleanup before deploying.
Look for internships that offer hands-on work with Linux servers, application deployments, cloud infrastructure, automation, or production monitoring.

Certifications can help organize your learning and demonstrate foundational knowledge. They should complement practical projects, not replace them.

blocks.text: If you choose a paid certification, verify the current exam, prerequisites, pricing, and validity directly with the issuing organization.

Further study can help you specialize in cloud architecture, distributed systems, or infrastructure engineering. For most entry-level DevOps roles, strong practical skills and projects can be more immediately useful than pursuing a postgraduate degree solely for the job title.

rows.text: Advanced cloud infrastructure and service management
Operating systems, distributed systems, and software engineering
Advanced technical study, subject to admission eligibility

blocks.text: Cloud certifications and hands-on projects are useful alternatives when you want to enter the workforce sooner.
Entry level — approximately 0–2 years
DevOps Trainee, Cloud Support Associate, Junior System Administrator, or Build and Release Trainee.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Linux, deployments, scripting, troubleshooting, and basic cloud operations.
Intermediate — approximately 2–5 years
DevOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer, Platform Engineer, or Site Reliability Engineer.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: CI/CD, infrastructure as code, container platforms, monitoring, reliability, and automation.
Advanced — approximately 5+ years
Senior DevOps Engineer, Cloud Architect, Platform Engineering Lead, or SRE Lead.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: infrastructure architecture, service reliability, security, cost optimization, and technical leadership.

These timelines are indicative, not guaranteed. Progress depends on the complexity of your work, troubleshooting ability, reliability practices, and the responsibilities available in your organization.

blocks.label: Platform engineering
blocks.text: Self-service tools and standardized infrastructure for development teams.

blocks.label: GitOps
blocks.text: Managing infrastructure and application deployments through version-controlled configuration.

blocks.label: Infrastructure automation
blocks.text: Provisioning and maintaining environments through code.

blocks.label: Observability
blocks.text: Combining metrics, logs, and traces to understand system behavior.

blocks.label: DevSecOps
blocks.text: Integrating security checks into software delivery workflows.

blocks.label: AI-assisted operations
blocks.text: Using AI to support log analysis, incident investigation, and operational automation.

blocks.label: FinOps
blocks.text: Tracking and optimizing cloud spending.

blocks.label: Cloud-native systems
blocks.text: Containers, Kubernetes, managed services, and distributed applications.
Build a strong foundation before specializing in advanced areas. Kubernetes, AI-assisted operations, and complex multi-cloud architecture are not prerequisites for every trainee position.
Career preparation checklist
0/12 complete
Year 1
Learn Linux commands, networking, and Git
Practice Python or Bash scripting
Deploy a basic web application locally
Year 2
Learn one cloud platform and its core services
Build and run Docker containers
Create a CI pipeline using GitHub Actions
Year 3
Provision a test environment using Terraform
Deploy and monitor a cloud-hosted application
Document a deployment failure and recovery exercise
Job preparation
Publish two or three complete DevOps projects
Practice Linux, networking, cloud, and troubleshooting interviews
Apply for DevOps, cloud support, and infrastructure internships
Reset checklist
For a B.Sc. Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics graduate, DevOps Trainee is a practical entry point into cloud infrastructure, automation, and software delivery.
Prioritize these five areas:

items.text: Linux and networking — understand how applications run and communicate.
Scripting and Git — automate repetitive tasks and manage changes.
Cloud and Docker — deploy and operate applications in controlled environments.
CI/CD and Terraform — automate testing, releases, and infrastructure provisioning.
Monitoring and troubleshooting — detect failures, investigate causes, and document recovery.

blocks.text: Your best first milestone is to deploy a small application using GitHub Actions, Docker, and one cloud platform, then add monitoring and document how to recover from a failed deployment. This demonstrates practical DevOps ability far more clearly than a list of tools on a resume.
